title: Capacity of the general two-way channel
formal: Determine \[F_{\mathrm{TW}}(W,\lambda)=\sup_{(R_1,R_2)\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{TW}}(W)}\bigl(\lambda R_1+(1-\lambda)R_2\bigr)\] for every finite-alphabet discrete memoryless two-way channel \(W\) and every \(\lambda\in[0,1]\), with both terminals allowed to adapt their transmissions to past received outputs.
why: Determines the fundamental value of interaction in simultaneous bidirectional communication.

progress.text: Shannon introduces the two-way communication model and capacity bounds.
The model notes explicitly preserve adaptive encoding and state that the general two-way capacity region is unknown.

definitions: The channel has nonempty finite input alphabets \(\mathcal X_1,\mathcal X_2\), output alphabets \(\mathcal Y_1,\mathcal Y_2\), and a table of arbitrary real probabilities \(W(y_1,y_2\mid x_1,x_2)\ge0\), summing to one over outputs for every input pair. In an \(n\)-use code, terminal \(i\) holds a message \(M_i\) uniform on \([K_{i,n}]=\{1,\ldots,K_{i,n}\}\), with positive integer message counts and independent messages. At time \(t\), its input is \(X_{i,t}=f_{i,t}(M_i,Y_i^{t-1})\), where \(f_{i,t}\) is deterministic and \(Y_i^{t-1}=(Y_{i,1},\ldots,Y_{i,t-1})\). Given the current inputs and full past history, the current output pair has distribution \(W\). Terminal 1 estimates \(M_2\) from \((M_1,Y_1^n)\), and terminal 2 estimates \(M_1\) from \((M_2,Y_2^n)\), by deterministic decoders. Error is the probability that either estimate is wrong, averaged over messages and channel draws. A nonnegative rate pair is achievable if codes along \(n_j\to\infty\) have error tending to zero and \(\liminf_{j\to\infty}n_j^{-1}\log_2K_{i,n_j}\ge R_i\) for both terminals. Thus \(R_1\) is the rate from terminal 1 to terminal 2, and \(R_2\) is the reverse rate. The region \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{TW}}(W)\) is the closure of achievable pairs. The law and all coding functions are public. There are no extra communication links, shared messages, input constraints or computational bounds. The received outputs provide the permitted feedback. Predetermined time sharing is allowed. The capacity region is compact, convex and downward closed, so its nonnegative upper supporting values determine it. Rates are in bits per simultaneous joint channel use, without an extra factor of two. The channel table and weight are mathematical real objects, not finite-precision algorithmic inputs.
answer_criterion: Supply an unambiguous real-valued function \(g(W,\lambda)\) on every channel and weight above and a Lean proof of \(|g(W,\lambda)-F_{\mathrm{TW}}(W,\lambda)|\le1/100\) everywhere. Certify both sides of the error in bits per joint channel use; exact determination also qualifies. The adaptive coding model must be retained. A finite set of examples, an uncertified plot or a restatement of the operational optimization or limit is insufficient. No specified formula syntax or polynomial evaluation-time bound is imposed.

sentences: Two terminals simultaneously communicate independent messages over one memoryless channel.
Each transmission may depend on the terminal’s own message and previously received outputs.
Reliable rates therefore include the possible benefit of adaptation and interaction.
The target gives the weighted upper support values of the complete two-direction capacity region.
The benchmark requires a Lean-certified absolute error of at most 0.01 bits per joint channel use for every finite channel and weight.

context_blocks.text: Both terminals send their own independent messages and receive the other terminal’s transmissions. Each may use past received outputs to choose its next input, making interaction part of the capacity question.

Shannon’s two-way channel model comes with lower and upper bounds. The historical model notes retain the general capacity problem as unresolved. The weighted upper support function records the full directional rate tradeoff.
